channel.title: PPCA on Insights for Action
channel.description: Recent content in PPCA on Insights for Action

item.title: Recreational Paddle to the breakwater
item.author: paul@insightsforaction.uk (Paul Hewson)
item.description: Don’t yet trust my knees to be stuck in a kayak all day, but this was fine. No problems getting out after the paddle, which means I’d have no problems getting out at lunchtime (which may not be as easy to negotiate as a slipway).

item.title: Rec paddle
item.author: paul@insightsforaction.uk (Paul Hewson)
item.description: Funny how sea kayak (and expedition kayaks) are now the standard. Highlight of the evening was a spin in the cave. Very calm conditions.

item.title: Sea Kayak rescue 4
item.author: paul@insightsforaction.uk (Paul Hewson)
item.description: This was a good week. A roll worked. I made a meal of a hand of god rescue because (a) big fibreglass boats are slippery and that threw me and (b) I was in front of the paddler. Second attempt was better, but need to watch both of those next time. I lost what momentum I had because the paddler was so far back.

item.title: Sea Kayak rescue 3
item.author: paul@insightsforaction.uk (Paul Hewson)
item.description: Another reminder to fill these things in as I go, I can’t remember what we did this week. I do know we got a few heel-hook rescues in. That all seemed to work quite well, and my back and forth technique (to avoid overloading the helper) seems to be fine.

item.title: Sea Kayak rescue 2
item.author: paul@insightsforaction.uk (Paul Hewson)
item.description: I think we did a bit of towing this week. Whilst I perhaps need to get a new towline (mine is 7m and was really bought thinking of GP boats at sea which never happens these days), but the Dupytren’s means I could really do with a Palm quick release hook thing.

item.title: Sea Kayak rescue 1
item.author: paul@insightsforaction.uk (Paul Hewson)
item.description: For the last few years, Adam has run four sessions on sea kayak rescue. They’ve always been very good, although I’ve never been able to attend all of them. This year, apart from the minor point that a doctor told me not to go, I’m available for all four.

item.title: A first trip on the lower lower dart
item.author: paul@insightsforaction.uk (Paul Hewson)
item.description: This was an informal session over by Jennycliff looking at some rescue and rolling. I haven’t been able to kayak due to a burst eardrum, so took the opportunity just to get on the water and see what my balance was like (very dependent on my eyes being open). Anyway, I’m going to plug the ear with cotton wool, vaseline and one of those commercial anti-swimmer’s ear plugs. I’m not giving up kayaking.

item.title: A first trip on the lower lower dart
item.author: paul@insightsforaction.uk (Paul Hewson)
item.description: I was really grateful to be messaged by Julian and encouraged on this trip. I’d kind of assumed it would be all intermediate level paddles by now, and didn’t quite feel I’d made the grade. I still don’t quite manage breaking in yet in a way I think is completely correct.

item.title: Returning to the lower dart
item.author: paul@insightsforaction.uk (Paul Hewson)
item.description: I’m pretty sure i did this paddle. There was a lot of water in the river. Either that or I did one much earlier in the season. I think we were at the limit of what you might encounter on a club paddle. No swimming (which I think really means I’m not trying hard enough).

item.title: Returning to the lower dart
item.author: paul@insightsforaction.uk (Paul Hewson)
item.description: I’m pretty sure i did this paddle. I know I did four on the lower dart, this must have been the fourth one. I should keep a better caleander (I’m writing this in August, planning for next year).

item.title: Returning to the lower dart
item.author: paul@insightsforaction.uk (Paul Hewson)
item.description: Well, I know I was on this trip because (a) my drysuit zip broke and (b) having collected my wetsuit etc., I promptly lost my car keys. Anyway, nobody seemed to feel the urge to throw me out of my kayak at any point and we had a lovely trip down the lower Dart.

item.title: Returning to the lower dart
item.author: paul@insightsforaction.uk (Paul Hewson)
item.description: So, this is a wild guess. I know for certain I did four trips on the lower Dart over the winter of 2025-2026. I think this was the first one.

item.title: Short paddle to Cable beach
item.author: paul@insightsforaction.uk (Paul Hewson)
item.description: So there aren’t many entries here because I’ve torn my meniscus. In fact, I finally saw an NHS physiotherapist today (13th October) who basically confirmed the problem. Anyway, I saw a post that there would be a short paddle, in calm conditions so it seemed too good an opportunity not to see how I got on in a kayak. It was definitely harder to edge to the left than the right, but I also think I could edge the boat using my hips if I really needed to. I didn’t get that completely figured out though.

item.title: Helping out on an introductory course
item.author: paul@insightsforaction.uk (Paul Hewson)
item.description: I volunteered to help with an Intro Course, run by Alan. He selected a few boats to use, I just had to help people fit the seat pegs and put on a cag and buoyancy aid. Note to self, the spray deck goes inside the cag. I also tried fitting people to paddles, I need to think about that again a bit harder, I think I got in the habit of using a shorter paddle as it kept me straight, but recently I’ve been using a longer paddle for the sea kayak.

item.title: Rockhopping to Cable Beach
item.author: paul@insightsforaction.uk (Paul Hewson)
item.description: This was a nice gentle evening, little swell, enough to make it not utterly trivial but light enough I could concentrate on manoeuvring. I borrowed a club boat again (maybe for the last time this season) and I am convinced the red North Shore Atlantic LV is lighter than my own, and turns more readily.

item.title: Lumpy Night in the Sound
item.author: paul@insightsforaction.uk (Paul Hewson)
item.description: I’ve not seen any photos. It was windy and interesting paddle. Dave had the yellow Atlantic and mentioned it feeling a bit tippy which made me feel a bit better. I had the red Atlantic LV as I had the week before, and found a missing washer from my kayak trolley (which needs gluing back on). We hugged the coast on the way out and I was looking forward to adjusting my footpedals at Mount Edgecombe again. However, this wasn’t to be. Pete decided to head out to the bridge, where there was a nice big swell. I make high tide 17:44 so that puts us there about one to one and a half hours after high tide (so that shouldn’t have made things too interesting). Nevertheless, we “surfed” back towards Drake’s Island on a big and messy swell (1.5 metres or more), and then cut across Winter and Mallard to get to Mountbatten. Maybe it’s good to be wedged in with tight footpedals in this weather? They feel right when I try it out, but I feel too wedged when I’m paddling.

item.title: Caves near Penlee Point
item.author: paul@insightsforaction.uk (Paul Hewson)
item.description: This was an interesting paddle. The conditions weren’t particularly challenging, but neither was it completely straightforward. We headed more or less directly to the East end of the Breakwater, taking a dogs leg to look at a cruise ship moored up (which was running a pretty busy taxi service to Phoenix Wharf by the looks of things). We then rock hopped along the outside of the Breakwater, which had enough swell to keep it interesting. Then we cut over towards Penlee Point, to have a look in a gully shortly before we would have got there. There were proper caves, you could paddle in far enough it would have been nice to have had a torch (it wasn’t pitch black, they didn’t go that far, but it would have been great to have a little help). We then went near Cawsand, but didn’t stop as it was too busy preferring the beach on the far side by the “tents”. We did a bit of rock hopping to Fort Picklecombe and then came home via Drake’s Island, Winter and the Mallard.

item.title: Rock Hopping Jennicliff
item.author: paul@insightsforaction.uk (Paul Hewson)
item.description: This was a slightly more challening evening, with swell over 0.5m, just enough to make the rock hopping interesting. It had definitely calmed down by the end of the paddle.

item.title: Gentle saunter to Mount Edgecombe
item.author: paul@insightsforaction.uk (Paul Hewson)
item.description: So my cunning plan was to borrow a club boat; it makes the difference sometimes between being able to attend and not. On this occasion I had a yellow North Shore Atlantic. This might be an important point, it wasn’t an Atlantic LV. I felt a little wibbly-wobby all evening.

item.title: Rolling practice with Adam
item.author: paul@insightsforaction.uk (Paul Hewson)
item.description: This was a little spontaneous, but Adam offered some “rolling” and “rescue” practice and I signed up. Warmed up with the usual T-rescues. Possibly identified a little flaw and I now have an exercise to work on, like a high brace recovery only I sweep. This is not so much about the start position, as getting used to having my back low to the boat when I go back into an upright position. At the moment, I still know what that feels like; whether I’ll understand these notes in a years time if I don’t keep up the practice in another question. Also, managed a couple of cowboy style self rescues (and a failed attempt, frustratingly I got myself back in the cockpit but failed to get my legs in). Practiced wet rescues (remember to make the most of edging my boat, rescued boat side down to get it on top, and rescued side up to help drain). Also, try to push boat into the right position first rather than turning it round. Did another rescue which would be appropriate(ish) if the paddler had a fractured collar bone (a bit like the one where you get in underwater and roll yourself back up, although you are dragging the casualty’s spraydeck to get them in before pulling them out). Went through hand of god routine (I nearly messed that up as I leapt too soon to grab the target boat). Also, spent a bit of time sitting on top of the boat behind the cockpit as a balance exercise. I’ve convinced myself I’m not in the market for a cheap fibre glass boat with a very small cockpit, but I like the balance practice, and will do more. Finally, rolling. Yes, I’m rolling. I need to take my time to rotate my body and set up, and be mindful off sweeping with the off hand position against the boat.

item.title: Heybrook Bay
item.author: paul@insightsforaction.uk (Paul Hewson)
item.description: This was an Adam paddle. There was a bit of easterly wind, so we followed the east side of the sound avoiding the worst of the swell. I did speak to some paddlers who had done a round-the-sound and they were claiming 2m swell on the west side. We had very little swell (maybe half a meter) and particularly round the south end of Jennycliff things were very tame. There was however a little bit more work to do in and after Rennie Rocks. There were places you could feel the effect of the wind (unusually, the Plym by Mountbatten was one of these), and that made paddling a bit more interesting.

item.title: Tuesday rec paddle
item.author: paul@insightsforaction.uk (Paul Hewson)
item.description: There didn’t seem to me a lot going on tonight, so I borrowed a G3 and joined Terry’s rec paddle group. It was fairly calm conditions, and I had a chance to chat with a few people. We followed the east side of the sound for a few miles.
